function.uniprot_function: Key downstream component of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway. In the absence of Wnt, forms a complex with AXIN1, AXIN2, APC, CSNK1A1 and GSK3B that promotes phosphorylation on N-terminal Ser and Thr residues and ubiquitination of CTNNB1 via BTRC and its subsequent degradation by the proteasome. In the presence of Wnt ligand, CTNNB1 is not ubiquitinated and accumulates in the nucleus, where it acts as a coactivator for transcription factors of the TCF/LEF family, leading to activation of Wnt responsive genes. Involved in the regulation of cell adhesion, as component of an E-cadherin:catenin adhesion complex. Acts as a negative regulator of centrosome cohesion.

pathways.pathway_role_summary: Beta-catenin is the central effector of canonical Wnt signaling. In the absence of Wnt, it is sequentially phosphorylated by CK1 (Ser45) and GSK3B (Thr41, Ser37, Ser33) within the destruction complex organized by AXIN1 and APC, leading to beta-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Phosphorylation-dependent APC binding (300-fold affinity increase, Kd 2-10 nM vs 0.6-3.1 μM) is critical for destruction complex function. Upon Wnt binding to FZD/LRP receptors, beta-catenin accumulates and translocates to the nucleus where it binds TCF/LEF transcription factors via ARM repeats 3-9 to activate target genes. Beta-catenin also functions in adherens junctions, linking E-cadherin to actin via alpha-catenin.

metadata.data_quality_notes: Comprehensive data available. Quantitative binding: APC (Kd 2-10 nM phosphorylated, 300-fold increase over unphosphorylated); alpha-catenin (15 nM); E-cadherin (85 nM estimated). GSK3B kinetics well-characterized (Km 8.5 μM, kcat 0.079/sec). TCF7L2 kinetics measured (kon 7.3×10^7 M^-1s^-1, koff 5.7×10^-4 s^-1). Individual ARM repeat boundaries from PROSITE and structural literature. Sequential phosphorylation mechanism well-established with strict Ser45 priming requirement. AXIN1, LEF1, beta-TrCP binding characterized qualitatively.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: Beta-catenin is the central node of canonical Wnt signaling. Key parameters: (1) Sequential phosphorylation cascade (CK1→GSK3B) with well-defined kinetics; (2) Phosphorylation-dependent APC binding shows 300-fold affinity increase, rate-limiting for destruction; (3) 12 ARM repeats create extended binding groove with specific determinants (Lys312, Lys435); (4) Dual function in adhesion (E-cadherin, alpha-catenin) vs transcription (TCF/LEF) creates compartmentalization; (5) Disease mutations at destruction box provide constitutive activation. Quantitative data enables mechanistic modeling of destruction complex dynamics and therapeutic intervention.
